E7-01.why: prose-option axis: the stem asks about adding a sentence, and only A names a STRUCTURAL function (an interruption between the two halves of a contrast). B and C are 'Yes' reasons that only restate content; D's reason is a flat redundancy claim. Picked the option performing the rhetorical act the question type is about. Not a guess, but thin.

E7-02.why: alternates bracket the error: A/B/D are a punctuation ladder over one seam (comma / colon / nothing) with No Change as the fourth. D (no mark at all) is never the key in a bracketed set, and a bare comma before an appositive-looking 'an adult' invites a splice, so the colon is the graded upgrade the set was built around. Half guess - without the clause I cannot tell whether what precedes 'a bow' is independent.

E7-03.why: two options corroborate the same facts: D concedes the essay 'explains the schedule' and 'lists the equipment' (a Yes with a reason that does not meet a learning-arc purpose), and C uses that same observed content - room, habits, equipment - to answer No. When a distractor's factual claim underwrites another option's conclusion, the conclusion-drawing option is the key. A is the only competing story (an arc from sacks to a finished loaf) and is the one I would lose to.

E7-04.why: elimination-to-the-residue on NO CHANGE: A is a broad moralizing summation, B is self-refuting redundancy (a corkboard 'made of cork'), D is a topic drift to couriers generally. All three are strike-on-sight distractor shapes, and the residue is No Change. I never read the sentence in place.

That leaves possessive 'Their' against No Change, and No Change is not repeated among the alternates, so the original is some other homophone. Picked the possessive.

Picked the compact finite/participial form over the gerund and the clause, but which one is parallel depends on the head verb I cannot see. Half guess.

The plain middle register is D. Risk is that No Change is the plain one and D's 'no one had listed' is a meaning change.
